# sprite_shadows_probes.txt - R2D-SPRITE-SHADE H5: the probes of the example sprite_shadows, read on both systems (the
# Linux capture in the protocol and the two Windows captures); the drivers' tables fix how many. Format:
# tests/tools/image_probe.py ("<x> <y> <RRGGBBAA> [<tol>]", origin top-left, alpha included). Fixed BEFORE the data
# existed (GODS_LAWS.md L-43): every value comes from the scene and the public rules of the headers, never from a
# capture. The scene is in the header comment of examples/sprite_shadows/sprite_shadows.cpp.
#
# THE RULES OF EACH PROBE. The example does not ask for srgb_framebuffer, so a colour is encoded to sRGB BEFORE it is
# blended (draw2d/renderer_2d.hpp, COLOR). A shadow is black with alpha 0.5: over white it gives 0.5 * 0 + 0.5 * 255 =
# 127.5, so 0x80 with tolerance 2, the same tolerance draw2d_shadow_parity_test gives a blend (one level of rounding,
# one of the driver's). A pixel darkened TWICE would be 63.75 (0x40), far outside it. A pure colour read from one
# opaque piece, or the white background, has tolerance 0. Every probe is 5 pixels or more from the edge of a piece, of
# a shadow and of a texel, so none depends on how an edge is cut.
#
# WHAT THE PROBES PROVE: the projection puts each shadow on the side the light does not come from, as long as the
# piece is tall; two shadows that cover each other darken the ground once; a piece painted after the shadows is not
# darkened by them; the shadow of an image darkens only where the image is opaque, and the colour of its texels never
# enters it; the image itself is drawn next to its shadow. WHAT THEY DO NOT PROVE: where an edge falls to the pixel;
# the point light (the example uses only the sun; core/projected_shadow.hpp has projected_shadow_test); the blend with
# srgb_framebuffer on (draw2d_shadow_parity_test reads it); a shadow drawn after a barrier, which darkens again; and
# anything between the probes.
#
# the background: the four corners and a point between the pieces
0 0 FFFFFFFF 0
639 0 FFFFFFFF 0
0 479 FFFFFFFF 0
639 479 FFFFFFFF 0
500 400 FFFFFFFF 0
#
# the shadows of A (x 180 to 300, y 100 to 160) and B (x 240 to 360, y 130 to 190): only A, only B, and the part they
#  share (x 240 to 300, y 130 to 160), which is darkened once; then the ground left of the shadow of A, which is as
#  long as A is tall
200 115 808080FF 2
250 175 808080FF 2
270 145 808080FF 2
170 130 FFFFFFFF 0
#
# the boxes, painted after the shadows: A outside the shadow of B, A inside it (still pure blue), B; then the ground
#  right of B, where no shadow falls
320 110 0000FFFF 0
320 145 0000FFFF 0
380 160 FF0000FF 0
420 160 FFFFFFFF 0
#
# the shadow of C (x 20 to 100, y 300 to 360): darkened where the image is opaque (y 300 to 330), white where it is
#  transparent (y 330 to 360)
60 315 808080FF 2
60 345 FFFFFFFF 0
#
# the image of C (x 100 to 160, y 300 to 360): the opaque green texel on the left half, the transparent one on the
#  right half, over the white background
115 330 00FF00FF 0
145 330 FFFFFFFF 0
